name: q-lint
description: Linting, Quick Fixes and syntax colouring for q/kdb+. Early version; catches the most common problems.

q-lint.enable.markdownDescription: Run the q-lint language server. Off, the extension keeps the syntax colouring and starts no server: no diagnostics, Quick Fixes, formatting or semantic colouring.

q-lint.serverPath.markdownDescription: Path to the `qlinter` binary. Left empty, the extension uses the server it was packaged with, and falls back to looking up `qlinter` on `PATH` when it was packaged without one.

q-lint.serverArgs.markdownDescription: Extra command-line arguments for `qlinter --lsp`, after the ones the other settings produce - for example `["--isolated"]` or `["--extend-select", "QS001"]`. Flags given here keep their command-line meaning, so unlike `#q-lint.lint.select#` they can widen what the repository's configuration selects.

q-lint.profile.markdownDescription: Which rules to run. Set here, it overrides `profile` in a repository's `qlinter.toml`; left unset, the repository's configuration decides, and `style` applies where there is none. `style` reports what q refuses and what q runs but is almost certainly a mistake. `general` keeps only what q itself rejects; `styleq` adds the conventions of published q style guides; `uqf` adds one repository's house conventions on top of those.

q-lint.configFile.markdownDescription: A configuration file to use for every document instead of the nearest `.qlinter.toml`, `qlinter.toml` or `pyproject.toml` `[tool.qlinter]` (the server's `--config`). Relative to the first workspace folder. Empty: the nearest one governs each file, as on the command line and in CI.

q-lint.lint.select.markdownDescription: Show only these rules, among those the configuration already turns on. Rule codes or prefixes, as `qlinter --rules` lists them. It narrows and never widens: a rule the repository's configuration leaves off stays off. Empty: no narrowing.

q-lint.lint.ignore.markdownDescription: Hide these rules in the editor. Rule codes or prefixes, as `qlinter --rules` lists them. Applied after the configuration, so it can only hide; the repository's configuration, which CI reads, is unchanged.

enumDescriptions: Lint the buffer on every change.
Lint when the file is opened and saved. Quick Fixes match the last saved lint, so they appear again after a save.

q-lint.lint.severity.markdownDescription: The severity the editor shows, by rule code or prefix; the longest that names a rule decides. For example `{"QS": "hint", "QE": "error"}`. Display only: what is reported does not change.

q-lint.fixes.unsafe.markdownDescription: Offer the editor-only Quick Fixes too: those `qlinter --fix` applies only with `--unsafe-fixes`, because they can change what a working program does or guess at what was meant. Off, only the fixes `qlinter --fix` applies are offered.

q-lint.format.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Format Document**, which applies the fixes `qlinter --fix` applies and nothing else. Off, q-lint does not register as a formatter.

q-lint.semanticTokens.enable.markdownDescription: Colour functions where they are called and parameters where they are read, on top of the grammar's colouring. Off, only the grammar colours.

q-lint.workspaceIndex.enable.markdownDescription: Read every `.q` file in the workspace at startup, never running it, so a name another file defines is not reported as undefined and is coloured as a function. Off, only open files are indexed.

q-lint.workspaceIndex.exclude.markdownDescription: Globs, relative to the workspace folder, of files and directories the workspace index does not read - for example `["vendor/**", "**/generated/**"]`. An open file is still linted and indexed. Version-control, `node_modules`, `target`, `dist`, `venv` and `__pycache__` directories are always skipped.

q-lint.trace.server.description: Log the traffic between VS Code and the server, for debugging the integration itself.
